author: cushag
text:
In the style that's old and true,
I tell you what my name's for;
Johnny I am and Mary too,
And we live together like a fur.


But our life ain't always so gay,
There are times when it's no fun;
For we have to cook and clean,
While our children run about and run.


So we say to them each night,
" Mind not what you do or don't ;
We love you all but we can't fight,
Or the house will fall down."

author: kemp_harry_1883_1960
text:
To-day I went to call on Miss Annie,

The little orphan girl, who lives by herself:
It is not often that one sees such beauty as hers;
I think she’s very good looking and well grown—and rich!

Assamese Poem

I am an Assamese, a land where beauty resides;
A land blessed with nature's bounty and divine tides.

The rivers meander through lush green plains,
As paddy fields stretch to touch the distant rains.

Tea plantations rise amidst emerald hills,
And orchids bloom in vibrant hues, like love spills.

In cities and villages, people live with grace,
With warmth and hospitality that lingers on their face.

From dawn till dusk, we celebrate life's essence,
In festivals and rituals, our heritage it blesses.

author: john_masefield
text: The poem "On my Mother's Walk" by Mary Jean Chan is an elegy that explores grief, memory, and the bond between parent and child. The speaker reflects on their mother's journey through life and death, using vivid imagery and poetic language to capture the complexity of human experience. The poem is structured as a series of monologues and dialogues, each reflecting different stages of the mother' s life and the son' s reflections on them. The son remembers his mother walking along a path near the family' s home, carrying him and talking about the meaning of life and work.

author: stothert_james_a
text:
But O! my Love, I shall not go to thee
With empty hand; and this I will bestow:

If I have made you sad or caused you pain,
Take from me all that I can do in vain :

And if I did no ill for which repentance
Might be a balm for aching wounded heart,

O let me make some little offering- gift,
Some sweet remembrance of affection’s part—

That thus when life is done, what man hath won,
What woman wins, may all be spent on love !

Reference: “The Man Who Was Tired” by Edward Shanks

The Three Little Birds
In a quiet row on the ground stood three small birds with wings unfurled. They gazed intently at a passing figure, and one inquired, “Does he think he can fly?” The others chimed in, shaking their heads in mock amusement. Their expressions brimmed with curiosity as they watched the man disappear around a bend.

text: The magnet of creation’s secret lies within my soul. Its presence draws me ever closer to this holy space where we meet beyond the boundaries of time and space. Here, I find solace for all my sorrows, a healing balm for all that aches within me. In these sacred moments, I am reminded of the true nature of existence—the eternal dance between the seen and the unseen realms. Let us cherish these divine connections, for they are but a glimpse into the vast expanse of cosmic consciousness awaiting our awakening.

I would not dare to own my love to thine;
Yet let me kiss thy hand, and kiss again,
Till it grows faint with kisses, till it fain
Would part from lips which know no other thing,
Save kisses, love for kisses, kisses divine!

O heart of stone! wherefore dost thou refuse
The sweet temptations of my gentle Muse?
Why will'st thou turn away, when thou canst hear
Me singing words so full of passionate fire ?

author: thomas_hardy
text: I was walking through an enchanting garden one day when I heard a chorus of bird songs echo through the trees. As I approached the source of the melody, I discovered a group of small children playing merrily nearby. Despite my initial hesitance, I found myself joining them in singing and laughing together. This simple yet profound experience reminded me that sometimes all it takes is kindness and curiosity to find true connection in unexpected places.

author: thomas_hardy
text: I was walking through a small garden near my house. There were many beautiful flowers around me. I enjoyed taking pictures of them because they looked so charming. Suddenly, I saw some pigeons flying towards me and landed on one of the trees in front of me. The flowers around started chirping happily and welcomed the new visitors. It was very surprising that even after being strangers to each other, they had been able to understand what I wanted to say and felt happy about it too!

author: william_wordsworth
text: The night sky has always been my haven from reality. Tonight is no different. The stars twinkle like diamonds against the black velvet canvas above me, their brilliance reflecting off the shimmering sea below. As the wind whispers through the trees around me, I can almost hear them singing sweet melodies of love and longing for home. With each breath I take, I am reminded once again how much I treasure this moment—how lucky I am to have found such peace amidst all these chaotic emotions swirling within me right now…
